policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads 'the priests' (hiereis); the mapped textual_variant note 'Some ancient authorities read the chief priests' places archiereis in the margin, so the ASV rendered the base reading.
ASV 'the resurrection from the dead' renders the prepositional ek nekron; the RP genitive ton nekron would give 'of the dead'.
English 'the number of the men' is definite either way; a Greek article on arithmos leaves no trace the ASV distinguishes.
hos and hosei both render as 'about' before the numeral; ASV 'about five thousand' does not distinguish them.
ASV 'their rulers' takes definiteness from the possessive; presence or absence of the Greek article is invisible in the English.
ASV 'elders and scribes' in the same possessive series; the article is not represented separately in English.
ASV 'gathered together in Jerusalem' fits en, but eis after a verb of assembling is regularly rendered 'in/at' as well, so the English does not settle the preposition.

ASV construes Annas as a new subject with the supplied verb — 'and Annas the high priest was there, and Caiaphas' — which requires the nominative series; the RP accusatives would continue as objects of the gathering.
The article with meso is not separately rendered; ASV 'in the midst' is the same either way.
ASV ends the address at 'and elders,' with no 'of Israel'; the RP addition would have to appear.
Noun oikodomon and participle oikodomounton both render as 'the builders'; ASV gives no basis to choose.
oude and oute both underlie ASV 'for neither'; the conjunction variant leaves no English trace.
ASV renders 'any other name under heaven'; the RP omission would leave the phrase out entirely.
te and de are both covered by ASV 'And' at the head of the verse.
Deliberative subjunctive and future indicative alike give ASV 'What shall we do'.
Present and aorist infinitive of arneomai both render as 'deny' after 'we cannot'.
ASV 'let us threaten them' has no cognate dative; the RP apeile apeilesometha would show as 'let us straitly threaten' or 'threaten with a threat'.
The article with katholou is not rendered, and ASV 'charged them' can carry the object over from 'called them', so the English permits the article, its omission, and the RP autois to.
Pure word-order variant; ASV 'answered and said unto them' is identical under either sequence.
Subjunctive and future of kolazo both give ASV 'how they might punish them' in the indirect deliberative clause.
Augmented and unaugmented pluperfect are the same word; ASV 'was wrought' does not distinguish.
ASV 'O Lord, thou that didst make the heaven' has the address followed directly by the participle; the RP addition would require 'thou art God, who madest'.
ASV renders 'by the mouth of our father David thy servant'; 'our father' is present and unitalicized, which the RP omission would not supply.
ASV opens the clause 'who by the Holy Spirit', rendering pneumatos hagiou, which RP omits.
ASV 'for of a truth in this city against thy holy Servant Jesus' renders the phrase RP omits.
ASV 'thy hand and thy council' gives a possessive with boule as well as with cheir, which requires the added sou.
ASV 'while thou stretchest forth thy hand' renders the possessive sou with cheira, which the WH/Treg reading omits.
Articular and anarthrous order both render as ASV 'the Holy Spirit'.
ASV 'of one heart' shows no trace of an article on kardia.
ASV 'and soul' likewise does not represent an article on psyche.
ASV 'aught of the things which he possessed' has a singular possessor matching the dative singular auto; RP auton would give 'the things they possessed'.
panta and hapanta are the same word for the ASV's 'all things common'.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'with great power' renders either sequence.

The variant only moves the genitive phrase; English must produce 'witness of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus' either way. The verse's textual_variant note concerns an added 'Christ', not this transposition.
en and hyperchen alike give ASV 'neither was there among them'.
ASV names him 'Joseph', transliterating Ioseph; the RP Ioses would give 'Joses'.
para and pros with 'the feet' both render as ASV 'at the apostles' feet'.
